body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: f7d8af70bec960f9acd62c123b969f4c3b613f6f -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you - a careful, well-argued fix, and the decision note explains the end-point-vs-line choice clearly.

### What looks good
- The tolerance is a point-to-point distance between chord END points only (`laws.rs` `proper_cross_touch`, `near` = `hypot <= CROSSING_TOUCH`); away from the other chord's ends the exact orientation sign stays the law, so the #1134 pass-through hole (a vertex a picometre off the other chord's interior) is not reopened - pinned by `a_walk_through_a_chord_at_a_vertex_a_picometre_off_its_line_still_warns`.
- `proper_cross` itself is unchanged, so `dist2_segs` and the arc-wall law keep the exact predicate; only law (a) reads the new one. One constant, one reader in the verifier; main's `crossing.rs` had no other touch tolerance, so this adds no second rule for the same question.
- Consistent with PR #1134's current rule (its `adaptive::guard` `TOUCH` = 1e-9, end points only), so the planner and the verifier will agree; the two PRs touch different crates and do not conflict.
- Units: the sim CL is mm throughout (no inch path in `crates/sim`), so 1e-9 mm is absolute in every document unit setting.
- Pins check the bucketed law against the all-pairs reference, assert the old predicate really tripped, and pin the 2e-9 edge. No existing test, golden or `crossing_buckets` assertion changed.
- Provenance and gate map on the new suite; `laws.rs` 395 lines.

### Local results (trial-merged with `origin/main` 890de463, clean merge, Windows debug)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-sim --lib` | 94 passed |
| `crossing_touch` | 5 passed |
| `crossing_buckets` | 3 passed |
| app `verify` | 21 passed, 2 ignored |
| app `golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| app `solid_law_goldens` | 5 passed |
| app `trochoid_op` | 5 passed |
| app `verify_arc_reading` | 7 passed |
| app `carried_verify` | 8 passed |
| app `warned_moves` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Reviewer probes (throwaway local test, not pushed; pairs reported, bucketed == all-pairs in every case):
- Proper crossing 1e-6 / 1e-8 / 1e-9 / 1e-10 mm short of a chord's end (other chord's ends 1 mm away), at x 0 and 1e4 mm: **reported** at every distance.
- Crossing whose own start stands d from the other's end: reported at 1e-6, 1e-8, 2e-9, 1e-9 (rounded just over); excused at 5e-10 and 1e-10 - i.e. only a sub-picometre fan at a shared vertex.
- 1e4 mm move crossed 1e-6 and 5e-10 mm from its far end: reported.
- A 1e-10 mm move at a chord's end beside a real crossing 1e-4 mm from that end: crossing reported; a 1e-10 mm move crossing another chord's interior: reported (tiny moves do not blur their neighbourhood).
- T-junction and collinear overlap: no crossing (unchanged from the exact law).
- NaN, infinite and zero-length chords: no panic, no crossing (same as before).

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Nearly parallel moves leaving a shared vertex a rounding apart read as a touch even when they diverge afterwards (probe: A (0,0)-(10,0), B (0,1e-10)-(20,-1e-6) - the exact law reported it, this does not). This is the same reading an exactly shared vertex always had (a fan from one vertex, not a pass-through), and the decision note's "no new class of miss" covers it; mentioned only so the maintainer sees it.
2. When #1134 lands, motion will carry its own `TOUCH = 1e-9` mirroring `CROSSING_TOUCH` (motion presumably cannot depend on sim). A small cross-crate pin (a test asserting the two are equal) would keep them from drifting - a follow-up, not for this PR.

Not exercised: release `--ignored` heavy lanes, UI suites (no UI change), the motion planner (untouched).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
